title: Deontic Hindsight: kellett volna and nem szabadott volna

sections.title: Unfulfilled Past Obligations
sections.content: To state what should have happened (but did not), Hungarian combines the past tense 'kellett' with the conditional particle 'volna' and an infinitive: 'szólni kellett volna' (one should have spoken). When specifying whose duty it was, the person takes the dative case (-nak/-nek) and the infinitive takes personal possessive endings: 'Neked szólnod kellett volna' (You should have spoken).

sections.title: Violated Past Prohibitions
sections.content: To state that something should NOT have been allowed or done in the past, use 'nem szabadott volna' + infinitive: 'Nem szabadott volna elhallgatni az igazságot' (The truth should not have been concealed).

sections.title: Past Obligation and Prohibition
rows: Kórházba kellett volna vinni a beteget.
The patient should have been taken to hospital.
Az orvosnak erélyesebben kellett volna fellépnie.
The doctor should have acted more forcefully.
Nem szabadott volna halogatni a műtétet.
The surgery should not have been postponed.
You needn't have worried (it wasn't necessary).

items.spanish: Már az első tüneteknél szakorvoshoz kellett volna fordulniuk.
items.english: They should have turned to a specialist already at the first symptoms.

items.spanish: Nem szabadott volna figyelmen kívül hagyni a magas lázat.
items.english: The high fever should not have been ignored.

items.spanish: Nekünk is óvatosabbnak kellett volna lennünk a kezelés során.
items.english: We too should have been more cautious during the treatment.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Contrast 'nem szabadott volna' (ought not to have done—it was wrong) with 'nem kellett volna' (needn't have done—it was unnecessary).
